title: Hyundai launches Neira three-row EV in Indonesia
summary: Three months after showcasing the Neira as a near-production prototype at GIIAS 2026, Hyundai has launched its final version at Gaikindo AutoWeek (GAW) 2026. The Neira is the company's first locally produced seven-seat EV in the country.

title: BYD starts deploying Flash Chargers in Malaysia
summary: BYD has deployed its first Flash Chargers in Malaysia, coinciding with the launch of the new Denza D9 featuring the second-generation Blade battery that can take advantage of the latest infrastructure. Access to these megawatt chargers will soon be offered to all EV brands.

title: New graphite could enable faster charging
summary: Researchers at Rice University in the US have developed a process that can produce synthetic graphite for fast-charging lithium-ion batteries in just 0.2 seconds. At the same time, the process could significantly reduce the synthetic graphite production energy usage and production costs of the anode material.

title: Suzuki Ignis Electric celebrates world premiere
summary: Suzuki's new electric microcar celebrates its world premiere. With it, the Suzuki Ignis name also returns to Europe. On the German market, the car will become the smallest fully-fleged electric car at 3.57 meters long.

title: Karsan to build 35 trolleybuses for Bologna
summary: Turkish manufacturer Karsan has won a tender from TPER, the public transport operator of Bologna, Italy. The contract initially covers 35 units of Karsan's new 18-meter-long e-ATA trolleybus, with a contractual option for 35 additional units.

title: General Motors to transition to native NACS charging ports in South Korea
summary: General Motors has signed an agreement in South Korea to adopt the North American Charging Standard (NACS) with Tesla. The deal extends an existing NACS agreement, which GM originally signed in 2023 for North America, to the Korean market.

title: Tata Group’s British battery cell factory faces delays
summary: There appear to be difficulties in the construction of the Tata Group's British battery cell factory in Somerset. According to media reports, a second construction contractor has already dropped out within five months. It remains uncertain whether the planned completion next year can be achieved as scheduled.

title: Electric Porsche 718 Boxster heads for series production
summary: The all-electric Porsche 718 Boxster is on the verge of series production, according to its German carmaker. It is set to become the most powerful 718 to date and will come standard with a switchable virtual transmission and a six-cylinder boxer engine sound. The electric Boxster is expected to make its world premiere in the first quarter of 2027.

title: Iveco Bus introduces new battery generation
summary: Iveco Bus is introducing a new generation of NMC batteries for its electric city and intercity buses. Depending on the model and configuration, these enable up to 100 kilometers of additional range. The manufacturer is also offering an optional battery warranty of up to 15 years.

title: British EVs could soon qualify as ‘Made in Europe’
summary: According to EU diplomats, EU member states are inclined to integrate British electric vehicles under "Made in Europe" guidelines. The European Union could apply similar credentials to the other states of the European Economic Area such as Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland.

title: BYD to acquire former Smart factory in Hambach
summary: BYD is negotiating with Ineos Automotive to purchase its plant in Hambach, France, as both companies have now officially announced. The fact that both parties are reporting on the transaction before finalizing the deal indicates the advanced stage of the negotiations.

title: Chery Group starts assembling Lepas EVs in Thailand
summary: Chinese conglomerate Chery Group has started assembling electric cars of its newest brand in Thailand, Lepas, beginning with the L6 EV. The company has an ICE L6 and a L6 PHEV also in its global line-up, but in Thailand, it produces and sells only the L6 EV.

title: VW and Elli launch €1,995 V2G BiDi wallbox
summary: Volkswagen and its energy subsidiary Elli will introduce their first Vehicle-to-Grid package to the German market in December 2026. The requisite DC wallbox will cost €1,995 euros. In addition to VW, VW Commercial Vehicles, and Cupra, Skoda will also be included in the launch. Details about the electricity tariff have also been announced.

title: Switzerland: VMCV orders up to 47 Yutong electric buses
summary: Swiss public transport operator VMCV has signed a framework agreement with Yutong for the delivery of up to 47 electric buses. The Chinese brand won the tender against three competitors. The contract is worth around 30 million francs, equivalent to just under €33 million euros.

title: Exicom to sell DC fast charger manufacturer Tritium
summary: Just under two years after acquiring the insolvent Australian fast charger manufacturer Tritium, Indian charging infrastructure provider Exicom is looking to divest the company once again. A non-binding agreement values the company at US$85 million.

title: Switzerland: Fastned, Obornes and Milence secure initial truck charging network
summary: The Swiss Federal Roads Office (FEDRO) has awarded the 32 locations tendered in January 2026 for the construction of a total of 82 truck charging stations along national roads to three companies. Lot 1 goes to Fastned, Lot 2 to Obornes, and Lot 3 to Milence.

title: New battery generation from Forsee Power: ZEN 8 now with 173 Ah LFP cells
summary: Forsee Power introduces the ZEN 8 LFP for light construction, agricultural, and municipal vehicles. The battery uses the same dimensions and mounting points as the ZEN 8 NMC, enabling deployment without changes to the vehicle design.

title: Infineon introduces power module for commercial electric vehicles
summary: Semiconductor manufacturer Infineon is expanding its portfolio with a power module for traction inverters in electric commercial vehicles. The new HybridPACK HD is based on silicon carbide technology and is designed for a service life of more than 1.2 million kilometers.

title: Fortum tests new battery recycling process
summary: For the first time, Fortum Battery Recycling has produced customer samples of nickel sulfate, cobalt sulfate, and lithium hydroxide in battery grade using its new recycling process. The materials, obtained at the Harjavalta facility in Finland, are currently being evaluated by potential customers.

title: BASF supplies CATL: CAM shipments from Schwarzheide have begun
summary: BASF has begun deliveries to CATL. The supply contract includes the provision of high-performance cathode materials from BASF's plant in Schwarzheide (Germany). CATL also receives battery materials from BASF in China.

title: EU introduces import quotas for hybrids from China and other countries
summary: It's official - from December, the European Union will introduce import quotas for hybrid cars from China, as well as restrict imports from other countries. The regulation will initially apply for 200 days, limiting the import of hybrid cars from China to exactly 191,780 units during this period.

title: Škoda Group restructures its rail, bus and drivetrain businesses
summary: Škoda Group is reorganising its business to improve efficiency and place greater emphasis on its products and services. As part of the changes, Škoda Vagonka will be integrated into existing subsidiary Škoda Transportation, while Škoda Electric will be split into two joint-stock companies. Further changes are planned for 2027.

title: No more factory teams: Stellantis exits motorsport
summary: Stellantis has exited the WEC and bid farewell to Formula E. This marks a radical shift for the group's motorsport strategy, especially considering Opel's newly developed Gen4 race car and the group's original commitment until 2030. Citroën must also say goodbye to Formula E, and in the WEC, Peugeot's recently updated 9X8 will not race. Here's how Stellantis plans to move forward.

title: ACEA: battery-electric cars capture 30 per cent of EU passenger car market
summary: In the EU, more than 250,000 pure electric cars are now hitting the roads each month. In October, this figure reached 280,000 units, a substantial increase of 61 per cent year-on-year. Across the EU's overall passenger car market, the share of EVs climbed to nearly 30 per cent.

title: VW starts production of the long wheelbase ID. Buzz Cargo
summary: Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles has started series production of the long wheelbase ID. Buzz Cargo at its main Hanover plant. The long version of the electric transporter, which has been available to order since September, offers 4.4 cubic meters of cargo volume, an 86-kWh battery, and a range of up to 490 km.

title: ‘The big advantage for us lies in flexibility’ – Electra manager Paul Tonini on battery storage
summary: Electra is increasingly relying on battery storage systems for its fast-charging parks. In Germany alone, 20 storage systems are already installed, and this number is expected to reach around 40 by the end of the year. In this interview, Germany CEO Paul Tonini explains the advantages of the technology, why grid operators sometimes complicate its deployment, and why battery storage alone cannot solve the challenges of expanding the charging network.

title: Fraunhofer explores lighter fuel cell bipolar plates
summary: The Fraunhofer Institute for Machine Tools and Forming Technology (IWU) has developed new manufacturing processes for particularly lightweight bipolar plates made of carbon fiber-reinforced plastic. The technology could make fuel cells for drones, small aircraft, and helicopters lighter and more compact in the future.

title: Mercedes receives KBA approval for door-to-door driving assistant
summary: Mercedes-Benz has become the first automaker in Germany to receive regulatory approval for a point-to-point driving assistant. The German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) approved the MB.Drive Assist Pro system based on UN Regulation R171. This enables automated door-to-door driving at SAE Level 2, including complex urban traffic situations.

title: Siemens introduces DC contactor for megawatt charging
summary: Siemens is expanding its DC portfolio with a high-performance DC contactor for voltages up to 1,500 volts and currents up to 600 amperes. The new SIRIUS 3QC1 combines semiconductor technology with mechanical contacts and is intended for use in megawatt charging stations for commercial vehicles.

title: Court deems BYD Ti7 too similar to JLR Defender
summary: A Dutch court has ordered ten BYD subsidiaries in interim proceedings to refrain from building and selling the Ti7 in the EU. According to the judges, the model looks too similar to the JLR Defender. However, the main trial is still pending.

title: UK energy price cap increase could add up to £9 to EV charging costs
summary: Charging an electric car at home could become noticeably more expensive in the UK from January, as a sharp rise in energy prices threatens to erode some of the cost advantages of running an EV. The impact will depend heavily on the driver's energy supplier and tariff, with households on standard variable deals facing the biggest immediate challenge.

title: EU postpones discussion on Tesla Assisted Driving
summary: EU-wide approval of Tesla's driver assistance system, Tesla Assisted Driving (TAD), is set to face further delays. A meeting of the relevant EU expert committee which was first scheduled for December 1 has now been postponed to December 15.

title: KAIST aims to extend the lifespan of anode-free batteries
summary: Researchers at the South Korean Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST) have developed an approach to extend the lifespan of anode-free lithium-metal batteries. They are leveraging a manufacturing process from the semiconductor industry and a coating just ten nanometers thick.

title: Volvo A40 Electric begins first construction site deployment
summary: Four electric articulated haulers of the Volvo A40 Electric type have begun their first construction site deployment at the British infrastructure project Lower Thames Crossing. The vehicles can each transport up to 39 tonnes of construction material. The charging electricity is generated on-site from green hydrogen.

title: BMW to roll out a new software update in December
summary: BMW provides over-the-air updates to 16 million vehicles in 88 countries and is set to roll out version 11/2026.3 of its software in December. The update introduces 24 new and revised features for assistance, navigation, charging, infotainment, and comfort.

title: Xiaomi prepares for EU market launch with test drives across Europe
summary: Xiaomi is pushing ahead with its plans to enter the European market in 2027 and has named Sweden, Germany, Spain, and Italy as test countries. Testing and coordination for the European market will take place at a total of seven locations, including Arjeplog in Sweden and the Nürburgring in Germany. Meanwhile, the operating loss of the vehicle, AI, and other new initiatives division increased further in the third quarter of 2026.

title: Budget exhausted: Spain cuts purchase subsidies for electric cars
summary: In Spain, the budget for the Auto+ subsidy program for private individuals has been exhausted. The government has allocated €350 million in purchase incentives for electric cars and plug-in hybrids in a short period. What's more, with parliamentary elections approaching in Spain, the funding pot will not be replenished for the foreseeable future.

title: Electric trucks in Europe: Why manufacturers are slowing down, and the ICCT remains optimistic
summary: The market ramp-up of electric trucks has been delayed by five years, according to European manufacturers. This was evident from the 'Cleanroom' discussions at the German Federal Ministry of Transport. At the same time, the International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT) paints a significantly more optimistic picture. A contradiction? Not necessarily. The two perspectives primarily highlight how heavily the development of the electric truck market depends on regulation, economic viability, and infrastructure.

title: ‘Internova’: Solaris coins new name for regional and intercity buses
summary: Solaris has revealed the name of its new zero-emission bus platform for intercity and regional transport. The battery-electric and hydrogen-powered vehicles, expected to make their world debut at Busworld 2027, will be marketed under the name Internova.

title: UK’s East Midlands region invests in 189 electric buses
summary: The UK's East Midlands region has been granted a £47.55 million investment for 189 battery-electric buses to replace older diesel vehicles. The region's Mayor is driving the government investment with further proposed contributions from Arriva, Stagecoach, Nottingham City Transport, and Trentbarton, with four schemes worth more than £100m in total.

title: Why China’s electric cars are parking back and forth
summary: In Chinese parking garages, electric cars have recently been seen parking and unparking themselves hundreds of times. Behind this curious phenomenon is apparently a competition by tech giant Huawei with some absurd consequences.

title: Hyundai launches Neira three-row EV in Indonesia
